proposed_core_edits.reason: The construction should select the global residual minimizer over a fixed isolating ball without assuming its uniqueness.  The revised branchwise proof derives local singleton existence from the full-rank score contraction and a compact residual gap; possible nonzero-residual local minima elsewhere in the ball cannot be selected globally near the population moment.

prose_updates.tldr: Three independent Gaussian snapshots have an exact dimension-dependent identification frontier under one unknown common positive-definite measurement covariance.  When \(p=2\) and \(d_0\ne0\), the two raw \(O(1)\) completions have opposite determinants and the negative-determinant completion fails the principal-logarithm cut, so model-compatible laws identify the full explanation.  The exceptional \(d_0=0\) regime retains a continuous \(O(2)\) ambiguity.  For \(p\ge3\), three snapshots generically retain a continuous \(O(p-1)\) ambiguity, whereas a fourth snapshot generically identifies through \(K_1K_0^{-1}\).  The four-snapshot block Gram certificate enumerates the raw stabilizer fiber; stability, the logarithm cut, Stein reconstruction, and strict noise positivity then determine exact structural compatibility.  Stabilizer dimension equals information nullity, and the sharp finite-fiber maximum is \(2^{p-1}\).  On each specified regular finite branch, a fixed-ball global residual projection is uniquely selected near the population moment and supports Gaussian moment inference, although a data-based global initializer and stable labeling rule across all noncyclic branches remain open.

sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Sample means and covariances form \(\widehat z\).  On the cyclic chart, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}\) and \(\widehat\theta_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\theta(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}},\widehat z)\).  For a specified regular noncyclic population branch, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{loc}}\) is the global least-squares residual minimizer over a fixed isolating ball; the theorem proves that this argmin is a singleton and smooth for moments sufficiently near the population law, so extraneous nonzero-residual local minima are not selected.  Globally certified data-based initialization and labeling across all finite branches remain the explicit open question.

prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The exact population conditions--spectral matching, block Gram equality, and the three-snapshot whitened norm equality--must not be imposed as empirical accept-or-reject equalities, because unconstrained noisy sample moments satisfy them with probability zero.  On the cyclic chart, \(\widehat W_{\mathrm{cyc}}=\widehat K_1\widehat K_0^{-1}\) is an off-model rational estimator; \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{rec}}\) guarantees that its full reconstruction is defined and \(\epsilon_{\mathrm{adm}}\) additionally preserves reconstructed-covariance positivity.  On a specified regular noncyclic finite branch, the local estimator is the global residual minimizer over a fixed population-centered isolating ball.  Full column rank of the residual derivative yields a contraction-selected stationary point, while compact separation of the sole population root from the complement forces every nearby global minimizer into that contraction neighborhood and makes it unique.  This removes dependence on arbitrary local optima but does not make the estimator a globally implementable branch finder: the isolating ball and branch label remain population-indexed until the certification question is solved.  No empirical exact spectrum, exact probe Gram matrix, or exact raw residual equality is required.
prose_updates.honest_scope: The theorem-level deliverables are the exact three-snapshot norm certificate and \(O(p-r)\) fibers, the dimension-two determinant elbow, the dimension-dependent three-versus-four frontier, the four-snapshot block certificate and admissibility bijection, the sharp attainable finite-stratum maximum \(2^{p-1}\), the information-nullity identity, cyclic perturbation bounds, and a population-branch-indexed local Gaussian limit law under \(\gamma_W>0\).  For the local limit, the estimator is a fixed-ball global residual projection whose singleton existence and smoothness are proved only on a sufficiently small neighborhood of the chosen regular branch; the result does not assume that an arbitrary local optimizer is the desired branch.  Three snapshots generically identify model-compatible systems when \(p=2\), except on the \(d_0=0\) continuous-ambiguity locus, while a fourth snapshot is generically necessary for \(p\ge3\) and generically sufficient on the cyclic chart.  A larger unknown-common-noise model inherits the deterministic Gaussian subclass's continuous nonidentification witnesses, not its dimension-two identification conclusion.  The global certified initializer, exhaustive branch certificate, stable empirical labeling, and simultaneous coverage across all noncyclic finite branches remain open; no uniform inference is claimed at branch collisions, positivity boundaries, logarithm cuts, or stabilizer-dimension jumps.

statement_notes.justification: Regular finite fibers require inference for every specified explanation rather than a standard error attached to an arbitrary local optimum.  The fixed-ball global criterion and compact residual gap make the population-indexed branch selector unique near the law.
statement_notes.gap: MorimotoKashima2025 provides an iterative fit and AaltoLamolineGoncalves2022 provides local sensitivity, but neither proves that a fixed isolating-ball global residual projection is the unique smooth selector near each regular common-noise branch or derives its Gaussian plug-in law.
statement_notes.consumer: Applied users who have a certified population branch neighborhood can report a confidence region for that explanation without silently selecting a spurious nonzero-residual local minimum; global discovery and labeling of all such neighborhoods remains separate.
